question: Sleep scientists say the most powerful way to reset your body clock after a long flight is not a pill or coffee. It's free and comes from the sky. What is it?
source_excerpt: Getting light in the morning will advance your body clock, while light exposure in the early evening will delay it.

extra.why_interesting: Players expect the best jet-lag cure to be a pill, coffee or a clever sleep trick. The answer is free and obvious once heard: going outside into the daylight.
extra.verification_notes: Light exposure (daylight) is the established strongest circadian zeitgeber for jet lag; no contradicting or newer info found, though I found no CDC or Sleep Foundation page and relied on secondary sources.

explanation: Light hitting your eyes is the main signal your brain uses to set its internal clock. A morning walk outside at your destination does more than any gadget or pill.

question: Your body clock naturally runs a little longer than 24 hours, so staying up late is easier for it than going to bed early. Knowing that, which direction of flight usually brings the worse jet lag?
topic: Jet lag and the body clock
source_excerpt: human circadian rhythms, on average, extend slightly beyond 24 hours

extra.why_interesting: Most travellers assume jet lag is the same either way, or blame only the number of time zones. Once they know the body clock runs a little long, they can work out on their own that losing hours by flying east is the harder direction.
extra.verification_notes: Eastward flight requires advancing a clock whose period is over 24h, which is harder, so eastward jet lag is usually worse; a model study supports this (https://www.statnews.com/2016/07/21/jet-lag-worse-east-west/).

explanation: Flying east shortens your day and forces you to sleep earlier, which pushes against your body's natural drift. Flying west just asks you to stay up later, and your body clock already prefers that.
